problem:
A distance function $s(t)$ has values according to the table below:

| $t$ | $0$ | $0.02$ | $0.04$ | $0.06$ | $0.08$ | $0.10$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $s(t)$ | $0$ | $3$ | $5$ | $9$ | $13$ | $18$ |

Approximate the velocity ${s}^{′}(t)$ at the point $t=0.06$ using a backward difference approximation. Do not round the answer.

$\,\,{s}^{′}(0.06)≈$ {{field-1}}
worked_solution:
We use the backward difference approximation formula

$$
{s}^{′}(t)≈\frac{s(t)-s(t-h)}{h},
$$

 
at the point $t=0.06.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case, $h=0.02.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}^{′}(0.06) & ≈\frac{s(0.06)-s(0.06-0.02)}{0.02} \\  & =\frac{s(0.06)-s(0.04)}{0.02} \\  & =\frac{9-5}{0.02} \\  & =\frac{4}{0.02} \\  & =200.\end{aligned}
$$
